ranking.note: Raised from P3: removes an unneeded censorship/pinning hazard in 1p1c package relay, which this category ranks first, on par with the other acceptance-correctness fixes
Lowered from P2: policy expansion revisiting closed #27926 with no cited downstream demand, so it ranks below policy work with written user pull

inconsistencies: #36328, #36608 and #35286 all touch 1p1c package acceptance paths (reject-filter classification, submitpackage package relay, test-only package validation). #36328 changes the acceptance result semantics and should be reviewed first; the other two build on or test that surface.

#36367 clamps prioritisetransaction deltas to stop fee-sum overflow, and #36608's card also claims to fix a fee sum overflow with extreme prioritisetransaction deltas during package handling. Overlapping fix for the same defect: settle it in #36367 (the focused change) and drop or rebase the duplicate part of #36608.
#36608 is largely a p2p/privacy rework; only its submitpackage package-relay addition belongs to this category, so its band here reflects that slice, not the whole PR.
#36214 (cluster limit trimming during reorgs) tests the same cluster machinery whose arithmetic #36367 fixes; if #36367 lands first the test coverage is more meaningful.
result.notes: The list separates cleanly: four acceptance/eviction correctness or policy changes with stated rationale (P2), then tooling, policy expansion without demand, and test coverage (P3). No PR here claims a remotely triggerable DoS or a cluster-mempool blocker, so no P1 is warranted.
